before_snapshot.comment:
APPROVED Li-S BASE-DESIGN ENGINEERING RECONCILIATION, item15, 2026-10-18. Wickerts corrected SI, DOI10.1021/acssuschemeng.4c01782.s001 Tables S19/S21: use baseline B recipe with the existing150 Wh/kg-cell and1500-cycle reference, rather than technical T ingredients associated with500 Wh/kg. Per cell: Li4g, separator6g, cathode8g, electrolyte29g, pouch.13g, negative tab.12g, positive tab.069g. Detailed retained masses sum47.319g, conflicting with source46g average. Adopt47.319g as the explicit engineering mass basis (not a measured corrected source cell); no arbitrary rescaling of individual ingredients. At150 Wh/kg this is7.09785 Wh/cell. Cathode B perkg: sulfur.28, CMK3.22, PVDF.13, acetonitrile.044, foil.38, organic waste-.054; inputs1.054kg=1kg product+.054kg waste. Preserve process-specific energy and transport. Source PVDF binder uses the existing polyvinylfluoride supply as an explicitly retained cross-version fluoropolymer proxy; exact binder chemistry remains a coverage/model gap, not a verified PVDF route. Per-cell assembly/formation/factory requirements retain their source cell amounts and are divided by47.319g. Module408cells=19.306152kg plus.275Al busbar+.593bimetal+.085Cu+2.75PP+2.5steel =25.509152kg. Cell share is0.7568323713779275. The mobile capacity market normalizes exactly to1 gross kWh at.150kWh/kg-cell, with.120-.180 endpoints and paired waste masses. Future density factors remain the existing relative learning assumption with fixed recipe; this does not validate a future physical cell design, cycle aging or calendar life. Controls/cooling are treated separately under item13. Source average-mass conflict and future recipe evolution remain explicit gaps. This supersedes older24.971kg-module/46g-cell and500Wh/kg-composition statements below.
PREVIOUS NOTES (retained as history; the correction above takes precedence):
Source: Wickerts et al. (2023). Prospective Life Cycle Assessment of Lithium-Sulfur Batteries for Stationary Energy Storage. ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering. https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.3c00141. Manufacturing of Li-S cells was based on the work by Chordia, M.; Nordelöf, A.; Ellingsen, L. A.-W. Environmental life cycle implications of upscaling lithium-ion battery production. Int. J. Life Cycle Assess. 2021, 26, 2024– 2039,  DOI: 10.1007/s11367-021-01976-0 8. Note that the factory construction and operation is included in this activity, and not in the "1 kWh storage capacity" as it is in the supporting information.

CLIC_snapshot.comment:
C082 approved static engineering reference: ingredient-sum cell 47.319 g; the source 46 g average remains a distinct reported reference, not an error. 408 cells and 6.203 kg noncell material form a 25.509152 kg module. Assumed cell specific energy is 150 Wh/kg; module demand is 8.808643655832261 kg per nominal kWh. Factory allocation is 5e-7 operating-factory units per nominal kWh (7.5e-8/kg cell). Existing factory construction and corrected TJ-based utility quantities remain unchanged. Component suppliers are reused; this does not admit salt/template/foil-process revisions, a new system architecture, future learning or automatic resizing. Retained capacity uncertainty describes the existing source model; joint dependence is not certified. Older mass/energy statements below are retained as source history, not active future scenarios.
